internal.title: Incident Report: Elevated Error Rate in Checkout Service Due to Payment Service Flag
internal.body:
On 2026-11-08 at 11:43 UTC, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. Diagnosis identified the root cause as an error injection in the payment service, specifically linked to the 'paymentFailure' flag. This flag caused knock-on errors in the checkout service, raising its error rate to 40%. The flag was disabled at 12:03 UTC after approval, leading to a verified recovery with error rates returning to normal levels. No latency or resource exhaustion issues were found in the frontend service. The incident was resolved promptly after disabling the problematic flag.

Timeline:
- 11:43 UTC: Alert received for high error rate in checkout.
- 12:03 UTC: Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection.
- 12:03 UTC: Flag 'paymentFailure' disabled after approval.
- 12:03 UTC: Recovery verified with normalized error rates.

Actions taken:
- Disabled the 'paymentFailure' flag in the payment service.

This incident highlights the impact of feature flags on dependent services and the importance of rapid diagnosis and flag management.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment service issue
external.body: Between 11:43 and 12:03 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced failures during checkout. The issue was traced to a problem in the payment service that caused errors to propagate to the checkout process. The problem was identified and resolved by disabling the related feature, restoring normal service operation. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your understanding.

lessons.lesson: Feature flags that inject errors can cause cascading failures in dependent services. Rapid diagnosis and controlled flag management are critical to minimize impact.
lessons.applies_when: When a feature flag in the payment service is enabled and causes a high error rate in the checkout service.

action_items: Review and improve monitoring of feature flags that can inject errors.
Establish faster approval workflows for disabling problematic flags.
Enhance cross-service alert correlation to detect cascading failures early.
